newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy cabinet approves measure to boost car sales.
newsitem.headline: Italy cabinet approves measure to boost car sales.

text.p: The Italian cabinet approved incentives on Monday to scrap cars which are more than 10 years old in an effort to boost sales of new vehicles.
Prime Minister Romano Prodi told a news conference after a cabinet meeting the measures would be in force for nine months and would operate as discount for people scrapping cars and buying new ones.
"A contribution will be introduced for nine months for the purchase of cars and linked to the scrapping of vehicles which are more than 10 years old," Prodi said.
"The contribution will be paid in the form of a discount which the producers will make to the client."
Prodi said the contribution would be up to 1.5 million lire ($982) for vehicles with engines of less than 1,300 cc and up to 2.0 million lire for those larger than 1,300 cc.
The measure, which must still be approved by parliament, is part of an end-of-year decree which is itself part of Italy's 62.5 trillion lire budget for 1997.
Recent data has shown Italy's car market to be stagnating but with a slight, positive trend, according to Italian auto sector research group CSP.
CSP has been one of the leading voices calling for some form of government incentives to revive the depressed sector.

Shares in Italian car maker Fiat rose nearly three percent on the Milan stock market ahead of the announcement after Environment Minister Edo Ronchi said earlier the cabinet was likely to approve such a step. ($1=1,528 lire)
